value: Sulfoaluminate-belite cement: belite-rich clinker with calcium sulfoaluminate (C4A3S, Klein's compound) as the reactive second phase, made from limestone with industrial wastes (PFA, gypsum) and, where alumina is short, bauxite; iron-rich variants (SFAB) fire lower still

note: "reactions between limestone, PFA and gypsum to produce the cement clinker take place at only 1200-1250 degC"; Portland clinker about 1450 degC (p.144)
upper end of the printed 1200-1250 degC clinkering range

value: Chinese CSA cement: clinker with 35-70% C4A3S plus belite (usually below 30%) and 10-35% ferrite, burnt in a dry-process rotary kiln with preheaters and ground with varying gypsum to give rapid-hardening, shrinkage-compensating or self-stressing cements

note: manufactured and used successfully on an industrial scale in China for about 20 years (as of the 1999 original)
